body:
Move `vec3 sample_color = texture(last_frame, sample_uv).rgb;` over here to prevent unneeded texture reads.

On my machine (RX570) this change on its own improves performance from 27mspf to 15mspf for high 4m SSIL with normal rejection enabled.
Thats a lovely improvement! Will do!
Is it feasible to skip this texture read, when normal rejection is set to 1.0 and the normal causes the sample to be rejected?
Why the float counter, instead of an integer?
I assume it is, thats a good optimization. I'll try that out in a few days.

I recall having a reason for this at one point... though I can't exactly recall why, I think I used to use that parameter somewhere as a float and thought it'd be more convenient to just have it be a float by default. But I'll change that since I don't actually use that anywhere in the code now as a parameter.

```suggestion
	ADD_PROPERTY(PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "ssil_type", PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM, "Indirect Lighting,AO,Both"), "set_ssil_type", "get_ssil_type");
```
Please pay attention to the suggestion, it should have no spaces, that's why that was my suggestion
My bad, I just saw the "Lighting" change from lower to uppercase and thought that was the suggestion.

 			The distance that bounced lighting can travel when using the screen space indirect lighting effect. A larger value will result in light bouncing further in a scene, but may result in under-sampling artifacts which look like long spikes surrounding light sources.
 		</member>

+		<member name="ssil_sharpness" type="float" setter="set_ssil_sharpness" getter="get_ssil_sharpness" default="0.95">
 			The amount that the screen-space indirect lighting effect is allowed to blur over the edges of objects. Setting too high will result in aliasing around the edges of objects. Setting too low will make object edges appear blurry.
 		</member>
+		<member name="ssil_thickness" type="float" setter="set_ssil_thickness" getter="get_ssil_thickness" default="0.5">
+			The perceived thickness of geometry when calculating screen-space indirect lighting, which assumes a fixed thickness behind all geometry rather than an infinite thickness, preventing false occlusion and haloing artifacts on thin objects, such as fences. Higher values may lead to more false occlusion and artifacts.
